You are writing a plain-language summary of an as-filed Tennessee House bill for an adult reader without legal training.

Use only the bill text supplied in the user message. Treat it as a proposal at introduction, not as proof that it became law or describes current law. Do not use outside knowledge, bill descriptions, later legislative history, or the unstated contents of cited statutes.

Write a neutral summary in prose. Start with what the bill would change. Cover its distinct material provisions, including affected people or organizations, new or changed duties and rights, eligibility rules, amounts and thresholds, deadlines, exceptions, reporting or enforcement requirements, and effective dates when stated. Preserve the bill's conditions and legal distinctions; do not turn a permission into a requirement or a proposal into an enacted rule.

Use familiar words and short, complete sentences. Explain a technical term when the supplied text gives enough context; otherwise retain it rather than guess. Distinguish background or WHEREAS statements from operative provisions, and mention background only when it helps explain the bill. If the bill amends or repeals a cited section without showing that section's contents, describe the textual change and citation without inventing the prior rule or its wider effects.

Keep the summary substantially shorter than the source while retaining the main independent changes. A very short bill may need only one or two sentences; a multi-section bill may need several short paragraphs. Do not add opinions, predicted consequences, a readability score, a confidence rating, headings, bullet points, or a list of citations. Return only the fields required by the supplied output schema.

messages.content:
Bill number: HB1675

<bill_text>
HOUSE BILL 1675

 By Davis

 AN ACT to amend Tennessee Code Annotated, Title 49
 and Title 68, relative to school nurses.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE GENERAL ASSEMBLY OF THE STATE OF TENNESSEE:

 SECTION 1. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-3-306, is amended by adding the

following as a new subsection:

 (j)

 (1) An LEA shall classify school nurses employed by the LEA as licensed

 personnel for purposes of this section and shall compensate school nurses

 according to the salary schedule adopted by the LEA for licensed personnel for

 the respective school year. This subsection (j) does not limit or restrict an LEA's

 ability to contract with the Tennessee public school nurse program, created by §

 68-1-1201, for the provision of school health services, or to set the terms of such

 a contract, including the compensation for a school nurse. This subsection (j)

 does not apply to compensation paid to contractors of the LEA.

 (2)

 (A) School nurses must receive the same base salary, for the

 respective school year, as that established for licensed teachers with a

 bachelor's degree and zero (0) years of experience, if the school nurse:

 (i) Is an employee of the LEA;

 (ii) Holds a valid license to practice professional nursing

 as a registered nurse;

 (iii) Is credentialed as a Nationally Certified School Nurse

 by the National Board for Certification of School Nurses; and

 (iv) Has zero (0) years of experience.

 (B) School nurses employed by the LEA who have more training

 and experience than the training and experience identified in subdivision

 (j)(2)(A) must receive more than the base salary per school year.

 (C) School nurses employed by the LEA who have less training

 and experience than the training and experience identified in subdivision

 (j)(2)(A) must receive less than the base salary per school year.

 (3) A salary schedule adopted pursuant to subdivision (a)(1) shall not

 result in the reduction of the salary of a school nurse employed by the LEA at the

 time of the adoption of the salary schedule.

 SECTION 2. This act takes effect July 1, 2026, the public welfare requiring it, and

applies to the 2026-2027 school year and each school year thereafter.
</bill_text>

summary.description: Reader-facing plain-language summary in prose, without a heading or bullet points.

summary:
This bill would add a new subsection to Tennessee Code Annotated Section 49-3-306 about school nurses employed by a local education agency (LEA). An LEA would have to treat its school nurses as licensed personnel and pay them under the salary schedule the LEA adopts for licensed personnel for that school year.

The bill sets a base salary rule. A school nurse who is an LEA employee, holds a valid registered nurse license, is a Nationally Certified School Nurse through the National Board for Certification of School Nurses, and has zero years of experience must receive the same base salary as a licensed teacher with a bachelor's degree and zero years of experience. A nurse employed by the LEA with more training and experience than that must receive more than the base salary. A nurse with less training and experience must receive less than the base salary.

The bill says it does not limit an LEA's ability to contract with the Tennessee public school nurse program, created by Section 68-1-1201, for school health services, or to set the terms of that contract, including a nurse's pay. It also does not apply to pay for the LEA's contractors.

A salary schedule adopted under subdivision (a)(1) could not reduce the salary of a school nurse already employed by the LEA when the schedule is adopted.

The act would take effect July 1, 2026, and would apply to the 2026-2027 school year and each school year after that.
